title: Steady-state current drive for tokamaks
bottleneck: A tokamak's confining magnetic field requires a plasma current of millions of amps, which today's machines drive inductively in pulses, but a power plant must run steady-state for months. Non-inductive current drive using radiofrequency waves or neutral beams exists but converts wall-plug power to plasma current at a few percent efficiency, recirculating too much of the plant's output. The bootstrap current helps but cannot sustain the full current profile alone in most designs.
why_it_blocks: Without efficient steady-state current drive, tokamak power plants either pulse, incurring thermal fatigue and grid-integration penalties, or burn a large fraction of their own output just sustaining the plasma, erasing net electricity.
current_state: High bootstrap fractions above 70 percent have been demonstrated transiently, and spherical tokamaks promise higher bootstrap current. No device has yet sustained fully non-inductive operation at power-plant-relevant pressure and duration.
